remaining_limits: Separately labelled TRUSTED row: Remote-SSH runs a server and extensions on the remote that can drive the local client; it never qualifies the untrusted terminal or guest-served editor paths.
Workspace trust is disabled, folder-open tasks are allowed and the unsupported-glibc connection prompt is pre-answered Allow, for this disposable fixture only.
The guest is offline: the trusted host harness stages the SHA-256 pinned CLI and server archives; the extension's own download/copy path is not qualified.

Extensions: the three Remote-SSH VSIX packages are SHA-256 pinned and every installed file is checked against the package (package.json differs only by VS Code's __metadata; .vsixmanifest is the package copy). VS Code itself is identified by version/commit, not by an application bundle hash, and its application shared storage (~/.vscode-shared) lies outside the isolated profile.
Fixture-only keeper feature adds exactly one guest-loopback port (9091) for the pinned server port; ordinary guests do not have it.
Copilot/AI features are disabled in the isolated editor; marketplace, agent host, git integration and telemetry are offline or unavailable and not qualified.
Editor cleanup: VS Code can re-create its temporary user-data directory while shutting down after the harness removed it; helper and endpoint cleanup is what the report asserts.
One run per adapter/fixture (two boots, two editor sessions each); macOS ARM64 native only. Linux and x86-64 hosts, and fleet eligibility, remain unqualified.
